post_text: Welcome to Tikpal. We are building an all-in-one Hi-Fi home audio system for focus, calm, sleep, and pure listening. This page will document the road to crowdfunding: prototype notes, sound tuning, interface tests, design decisions, and community review. If something is still being tested, we will say so. Thanks for following the build.

post_text: Why bring the amplifier, DAC, speakers, streamer, display, and software together? Because the room experience depends on the whole path. Tikpal is being designed as one system so sound, source control, display behavior, and daily use can be tuned together. That does not remove tradeoffs. It makes them visible earlier.

cta: Comment with the system you listen to today.

post_text: Design Vote: ambient display density. We are testing three directions for the room canvas. A: Minimal - time, room mode, and a quiet playback line. B: Balanced - time, mode, track title, and soft progress. C: Detailed - more source and audio information visible at rest. Which direction feels most like a calm Hi-Fi object for the home? Vote A, B, or C in the comments.
media_brief: Three UI mockups showing minimal, balanced, and detailed ambient display density.

post_text: Sound Tuning Notes: early preset directions. The current prototype is exploring Flat, Warm, and Vocal listening modes. Flat is the reference direction. Warm is for comfortable low-volume sessions. Vocal is for presence and clarity without pushing the sound into harshness. These names are prototypes, not final claims. Which character do you usually reach for at home?
media_brief: Three simple EQ preset cards on a dark background.
cta: Comment with Flat, Warm, or Vocal.

post_text: Prototype Diary: streamer software. Tikpal is currently testing the software path that connects local library playback, radio, Spotify Connect, AirPlay, Bluetooth, and DLNA into one calmer control surface. Not every source behaves the same way, so the interface needs to show truthful states without feeling busy.
media_brief: Bench setup photo with Raspberry Pi, display, and listening notes.
cta: Tell us which source matters most to you.

post_text: Focus mode is not meant to be a productivity claim. It is a room state: lower visual noise, direct audio control when needed, and a display that can stay present without asking for attention. We are designing Tikpal so the room feels ready before the controls appear.

post_text: Road to Crowdfunding: Tikpal has a display, but the display is not meant to behave like a phone or tablet. The default surface is a room canvas: readable from a distance, low information, and calm enough to leave on during listening. Playback controls are still there. They appear when needed.

C: Ivory Studio - softer and lighter while staying restrained. Which one feels most at home in a listening room?

post_text: Sound Tuning Notes: impressions versus measurements. Listening impressions help us describe how a prototype feels. Measurements help us check whether a change is repeatable. Tikpal needs both. When we share tuning notes, we will separate what we heard, what we checked, and what is still not final.

post_text: Prototype Diary: source handoff. Library and radio behave like direct playback sources. AirPlay, Bluetooth, and DLNA behave more like intake paths: Tikpal opens the path, waits for a device, then confirms the connection. The interface should stay calm, but the status still has to be truthful.

post_text: The room canvas is the default Tikpal surface. It shows only what the room needs at rest: mode, time, playback status, and subtle progress. The idea is simple: daily listening should not require entering a settings screen, and the display should not compete with the music.

cta: Where would Tikpal live in your home?

post_text: Question: Is Tikpal just a streamer with a screen? Current answer: no. The streamer is one part of the system. Tikpal is being designed around the full room experience: sound path, display behavior, source handoff, playback control, and room modes working together. Some details are still prototypes, and we will keep showing the tradeoffs.

A quiet interface still has to tell the listener what is happening, especially when a source is waiting for connection.

If you could choose one physical or secondary control to prioritize, what would it be? A: rotary control. B: remote control. C: mobile controller. D: keep the main surface touch-first. Tell us why.

post_text: Sound Tuning Notes: low-volume listening. A lot of home listening happens below showpiece volume. We are testing how the prototype feels when music is quiet enough for evening, reading, or background sessions. The goal is not louder. The goal is useful balance at realistic volume.

post_text: Prototype Diary: modes versus playlists. Focus, Calm, Sleep, and Hi-Fi are not just labels for playlists. They are room modes: different combinations of display behavior, sound intent, brightness, source control, and listening context. This helps Tikpal feel less like an app menu and more like an audio object for the room.

post_text: Calm mode is being shaped as a softer room state: less visual density, gentler display behavior, and audio control that stays available without taking over the screen. This is one of the places where Tikpal's display matters most. It should support the room, not dominate it.

cta: When does music become background for you?

post_text: Fair concern: all-in-one audio can become a compromise if integration is used as an excuse. For Tikpal, integration is the constraint. The sound path, thermal behavior, display, controls, and serviceability have to be considered together. We will keep documenting those tradeoffs before crowdfunding.

post_text: Sound Tuning Notes: Vocal direction. The early goal is presence without glare. Voices should feel clear enough for attentive listening, but not pushed so far forward that long sessions become tiring. This is still prototype language, and the final curve may change after more listening and measurement.

post_text: Prototype Diary: brightness and night behavior. Tikpal's display needs to work in a real room, including evenings. The current direction is simple: dim the room canvas without interrupting the music source. We are testing how much information should remain visible when the screen is quieter.

post_text: Tikpal separates daily playback from device settings. Playback should be fast: play, pause, source, volume, track, and current status. Device settings should stay lower-frequency and harder to trigger by accident. This is part of making the product feel like a Hi-Fi object instead of a general-purpose screen.
